Of the current state governors, 8 are [Democrats](Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") and 4 are [Republicans](Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)").

[Madeleine Kunin](Madeleine_Kunin "Madeleine Kunin") is the oldest living former female governor at 89.

The first woman to act as governor was [Carolyn B. Shelton](Carolyn_B._Shelton "Carolyn B. Shelton"), who served as Acting Governor of Oregon for one weekend – 9 a.m. Saturday, February 27, through 10 a.m. Monday, March 1, 1909. Benson](Frank_W._Benson_(politician) "Frank W. Benson (politician)"), had gotten sick and could not assume office early. Chamberlain left Shelton, his secretary, in charge for the weekend.[[1]](List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-1) It was another three and a half years before women were allowed to vote in Oregon.[[2]](List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-Oregon_Historical_Quarterly-2)[[lower-alpha 1]](List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-4)

**Kay Ellen Ivey** (born October 15, 1944) is an American politician who is the 54th [governor of Alabama](List_of_governors_of_Alabama "List of governors of Alabama"), serving since 2017. Originally a [conservative](Conservative_Democrat "Conservative Democrat") [Southern Democrat](Southern_Democrats "Southern Democrats"), Ivey became a member of the [Republican Party](Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") in 2002. She was the 38th [Alabama state treasurer](Alabama_State_Treasurer "Alabama State Treasurer") from 2003 to 2011 and the 30th [lieutenant governor of Alabama](List_of_lieutenant_governors_of_Alabama "List of lieutenant governors of Alabama") from 2011 to 2017.

Ivey became Alabama's second female governor and the first female Republican governor upon the resignation of her predecessor, [Robert J. Bentley](Robert_J._Bentley "Robert J. Bentley"). She won a full term in [2018](2018_Alabama_gubernatorial_election "2018 Alabama gubernatorial election") by 19.1 percentage points against Democratic nominee [Walt Maddox](Walt_Maddox "Walt Maddox") and was reelected by 37.7 percentage points over Democratic nominee [Yolanda Flowers](Yolanda_Flowers "Yolanda Flowers") in [2022](2022_Alabama_gubernatorial_election "2022 Alabama gubernatorial election"). At 78, Ivey is the [oldest currently serving governor in the United States](List_of_current_United_States_governors "List of current United States governors").

## Early life and education

Ivey was born on October 15, 1944, in [Camden, Alabama](Camden%2C_Alabama "Camden, Alabama"), as the only child to Boadman Nettles (1913–1997) and Barbara Elizabeth Ivey ([née](N%C3%A9e "Née") Nettles; 1915–1998).[[1]](Kay_Ivey#cite_note-1)[[2]](Kay_Ivey#cite_note-2)[[3]](Kay_Ivey#cite_note-3) Her father, who served as an officer in the [U.S. Army](United_States_Army "United States Army") during [World War II](World_War_II "World War II"), worked with the [Gees Bend](Boykin%2C_Alabama "Boykin, Alabama") community as part of the [Farmers Home Administration](Farmers_Home_Administration "Farmers Home Administration").[[4]](Kay_Ivey#cite_note-4)[[5]](Kay_Ivey#cite_note-5)
